subject.title: [Bug] Gateway swallows user-visible reply when an agent's exec stdout matches "configuration file" — replies=2 puts ⚠️ 🛠️ first, the actual reply second

question: After a successful final agent answer, should an earlier or ambiguous mutating-tool error still be emitted as a separate user-visible channel warning, and if so under which confirmed-failure boundary?
rationale: The current record supports an already-fixed Feishu ordering problem but does not establish whether the remaining visible warning is an intended safety signal or a stale recovered-error leak. That user-facing policy cannot be chosen safely from historical logs alone.

options.title: Require confirmed terminal failure
options.body: Suppress warnings when the run has a successful final outcome unless the tool error is explicitly unrecovered or independently confirmed as a failed mutation.

options.title: Preserve current mutating warnings
options.body: Keep warnings for any recorded mutating action even after a successful final answer, accepting that successful turns may show a separate caution card.

options.title: Add a scoped policy after proof
options.body: First collect a current-main Feishu trajectory, then define a narrow recovered-error rule for the demonstrated error class.

recommendation.title: Require confirmed terminal failure
recommendation.body: Suppress warnings when the run has a successful final outcome unless the tool error is explicitly unrecovered or independently confirmed as a failed mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail places this person at the introduction of the shared failed-mutation visibility behavior that the policy decision would refine.
